rows.notes: aextract_data picks bill / bill/{congress} / bill/{congress}/{bill_type} by param branch (:268-288); limit=0 diverts to get_all_bills_by_type (helpers.py:234-309) which reads pagination.count and builds an offset-URL list fanned out via amake_requests. Rows from response['bills'] (:312); transform_data re-sorts client-side by latestAction/updateDate (:321) and pops the nested latestAction key into two flat fields.

Base bill GET (:99); up to 7 conditional sub-resource GETs (cosponsors/subjects/summaries/committees/actions/titles/relatedBills, :111-189) whose URLs are read from the base response and merged back into one dict. transform_data assembles a single markdown_content string from that dict, regex-converting summary HTML (:204-255). Output is one Data object, not a record list.

Not tabular JSON: the fetcher loops caller-supplied congress.gov/govinfo.gov document URLs (:78-85) and make_request each (:101); .pdf bodies are base64-encoded bytes (:105-117), non-PDF bodies pass through as response.text (:118-127). One result dict per URL, errors captured in-row. endpoints=0 because URLs are arbitrary caller-provided download links, no enumerable path set. UNMAPPED_SUGGESTION: document_body_passthrough -- pdf_bytes_passthrough covers only the PDF branch, not the plain-text/XML body branch actually read at :121.

List from response['amendments'] (:275) on amendment / amendment/{congress} / amendment/{congress}/{type} branch paths (:239-245). Every listed item then gets a follow-up GET of its own detail url via asyncio.gather (:280-288) and selected fields merged back (:290-308). limit=0 diverts to get_all_amendments_by_type (helpers.py:685-741), an offset-URL fan-out. transform_data client-side sorts (:319) and flattens latestAction/amendedBill/sponsors.

Base amendment GET (:103); conditional follow-up GETs of cosponsors/actions/textVersions URLs returned in the base payload (:114-136), merged into one dict. transform_data (:140-245) assembles a single markdown_content string plus raw_data; the body is one object, not rows (single_row_assembly is the closest existing label).

Not tabular JSON: loops caller-supplied congress.gov document URLs (:71-75), make_request each (:91); .pdf -> base64 bytes (:95-107), else response.text passthrough (:108-117); one dict per URL with inline error rows. endpoints=0 because paths are arbitrary caller-provided links. UNMAPPED_SUGGESTION: document_body_passthrough -- pdf_bytes_passthrough names only the PDF branch; the plain-text/XML body at :111 has no existing label.

Two independent sources gathered concurrently (:141-145): api.congress.gov/v3/committee/{chamber}/{code} detail plus the static unitedstates.github.io committee-membership-current.json keyed by a thomas_id derived from the system code (committees.py:16-35, :57-76). transform_data merges both into one markdown_content record; join stays false because neither request's result feeds the other's URL. Output is a single object, not rows.

fetch_committee_documents runs up to 5 doc_type-branched pipelines in parallel (:1149-1213): reports (:714+), hearings+details (:831+), meetings via HTML scrape of www.congress.gov/search then per-event API details (:415+, congress_search.py:16 with regex _parse_page), prints (:982+), committee bills (:159+). Each list endpoint next-URL paginates (:734,:862,:1007,:598); PDF URLs are constructed by template from citation fields (:248-251,:785-790,:941,:1075); results are congress-matched, deduped and subcommittee-filtered client-side (:1226-1250); responses cached in SQLite (:1134-1145) with OVER_RATE_LIMIT semaphore+backoff retries (:114-131). endpoints=10 counting the distinct /v3 paths listed plus the search HTML page.
